conventions.convention: The coefficient space is real. Wavelet levels start at l=0, with 2^l coordinates per level; a_l=2^l for l≥1 and a_0=2. Its squared norm uses weights a_l^(-1)(log a_l)^(-2δ). The trace is finite exactly for δ>1/2.

The product prior uses σ_l=2^(-l(α+1/2)), α>0, and supplied IID coefficients with finite second moment. Countable choice supplies completeness for the L2 specialization; an already complete abstract Hilbert space requires no additional choice assumption.

The full L2 posterior kernel is supplied model input. The selected version has the displayed product-coordinate Bayes marginals; the item verifies their conditional-law identities under the prior-predictive model rather than proving a general posterior-kernel existence theorem.

The truth satisfies sup|θ_0,lk/σ_l|≤M<τ. The density is globally bounded above, uniformly positive on (-τ,τ), and has finite second moment. Continuity at every normalized truth coefficient is additionally required for the BvM theorem, but not for the posterior moment estimate.
The posterior is centered at the H(δ)-valued observation X and scaled by √n. The bounded-Lipschitz test class separately requires supremum norm≤1 and Lipschitz constant≤1.

N(m,v) denotes the affine pushforward of the explicitly normalized standard Gaussian density, with v≥0 and N(m,0)=δ_m. Gaussianity of an H(δ)-valued random element means normality of every continuous real linear functional.

Finite-coordinate total variation is sup_A|μ(A)-ν(A)|. The stronger proved density conclusion is convergence of the full L1 distance; the empty coordinate set carries the unique probability on a one-point space.
The bounded-Lipschitz BvM conclusion assumes countable choice. Full AC is explicitly assumed for the separate tightness and weak-topology corollaries.

load_bearing.statement: Under its stated wavelet-basis, product-prior, supplied-posterior, countable-choice, density and normalized-truth hypotheses, for every δ>1/2 the posterior law of √n(f−X) converges to canonical white noise in the bounded-Lipschitz metric on H(δ), in probability under P_f0^(n).

Under the stated product-prior model, countable choice, supplied posterior kernel, bounded normalized truth strictly inside the density's uniformly positive region, global density upper bound and finite second moment, for every δ>1/2 there is C_δ<∞ independent of n such that E_f0^(n)∫||f−f0||_H(δ)^2 Π_n(df|X)≤C_δ/n. No continuity assumption on the density is needed.

For every fixed finite coordinate set J, under its supplied-posterior and countable-choice hypotheses, boundedness of the prior density and continuity and strict positivity at each normalized truth coefficient imply L1 convergence in probability of the posterior density of √n(θ_J−X_J) to the standard product Gaussian density, hence total-variation convergence.

In the stated product white-noise model with a supplied L2 posterior kernel, every finite coordinate posterior marginal is the product of densities proportional to exp(−n(t−X_j)^2/2) σ_j^(-1)φ(t/σ_j); every denominator is strictly positive and finite.

Assume countable choice. For the stated wavelet or trigonometric basis and supplied independent standard-density-normal coordinates, white noise is almost surely an H(δ)-valued Borel Gaussian random element for every δ>1/2. In infinite dimension it is not L2-valued. A continuous coefficient pairing with coefficients d_j has variance Σ_j d_j².

H(δ), δ>0, is the coefficient sequence space with squared norm Σ_l,k a_l^(-1)(log a_l)^(-2δ)|c_lk|². It is a separable Hilbert space, L2 embeds continuously and injectively by coefficients, and the stated weight trace is finite exactly when δ>1/2.

Assume AC. For Borel probabilities μ_n,μ on a Polish metric space, μ_n⇒μ if and only if β_BL(μ_n,μ)→0. The implication from bounded-Lipschitz convergence to weak convergence is choice-free; the reverse proof uses AC through Prokhorov's theorem.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 takes the expectation of a bounded-Lipschitz distance, and 3.1 applies Markov's inequality, without explicitly establishing measurability of the supremum over the test class. Separability of H(δ) permits reduction to a countable pointwise-dense family of bounded 1-Lipschitz tests; recording that argument would justify these operations for the supplied posterior kernel and clarify that no stronger choice assumption is being used.

seams_checked.note: The linear and nonlinear functional theorems explicitly inherit the product-prior theorem's basis, density, truth, supplied-posterior and countable-choice hypotheses. They use bounded-Lipschitz pushforward bounds directly, retaining the continuous-pairing requirement and the canonical Gaussian variance. The density-model results use the coefficient conventions with additional localization hypotheses stated separately; their uses of weak-to-BL conversion explicitly assume AC. No converse implication or stronger Gaussian topology is imported. The main source's Condition 1 and projection/tail argument were also checked in [Castillo–Nickl, §3](https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~rn289/Site/__files/AOS1133.pdf).
